amstar2_items.justification: The review frames three broad descriptive/thematic questions (factors determining emptying method choice, challenges faced by emptiers, and improvement initiatives in SSA, South and Southeast Asia) rather than PICO components with defined intervention/exposure, comparator, and outcome criteria; eligibility criteria are deferred to online Supplementary Table S1.
No pre-registered review protocol (e.g., PROSPERO or OSF) or statement that review methods were established prior to conducting the review is reported.

Section 3.2 reports that the 37 included studies comprised 17 observational studies, 10 practitioner papers, and 10 case studies, but Section 2 provides no methodological explanation or justification for selecting these designs.

Although five databases were searched (Web of Science, Environmental Complete, Scopus, Global Health, and PubMed) and search terms are referenced in online Supplementary Table S2, the authors do not justify restricting the search to English-language publications or the 2002-2021 window, nor do they explain how grey/practitioner reports cited among the included studies entered a purportedly peer-reviewed search.
Title/abstract and full-text screening are described in the passive voice without reporting independent duplicate screening or consensus procedures.
Extracted variables are listed in Section 2, but there is no indication that data extraction was performed in duplicate or verified by a second reviewer.

Section 3.1 reports that 94 of 131 full-text articles were excluded, but no list of excluded full-text studies with study-level reasons for exclusion is provided in the article or referenced in the Supplementary Material.

No study-level Characteristics of Included Studies table is printed in the PDF (or referenced in the Supplementary Material, which only cites Tables S1 and S2); only aggregate frequency charts (Figures 2-5) and selective narrative examples are provided.
No risk-of-bias or critical appraisal tool was applied to any of the 37 included observational, case-study, or practitioner publications.
Sources of funding for the included primary studies are not systematically reported or discussed in the review.
No quantitative meta-analysis was performed; synthesis is limited to descriptive paper counts and thematic narrative discussion.
No meta-analysis or risk-of-bias assessment was conducted.

Because no quality or risk-of-bias appraisal was conducted, study-level methodological limitations (including reliance on unappraised grey reports, theses, and practitioner briefings) are not accounted for when interpreting findings.

While the narrative notes contrasting findings on manual versus mechanical emptying costs (e.g., Bangladesh and Kisumu versus other settings) and broad regional cost differences between SSA and Asia, methodological and design heterogeneity across observational studies, practitioner notes, and theses is not systematically investigated.
No quantitative synthesis was performed, and publication bias was not assessed.

The Conflict of Interest statement explicitly declares that the research was conducted in the absence of any commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.

raw_response.methodological_notes: Although self-described as a PRISMA systematic review of peer-reviewed journals (Jan 2002-Dec 2021) with 37 included articles, the review functions methodologically as a descriptive scoping/thematic mapping synthesis (counting frequency of themes across 17 observational studies, 10 practitioner papers, and 10 case studies, with zero risk-of-bias appraisal). Three major internal reporting anomalies affect primary-study tracking: (1) No Characteristics of Included Studies table or list of the 37 included studies is printed in the PDF (nor is one cited in the Supplementary Material, which only references Tables S1 and S2 for eligibility criteria and search terms), and Results Section 3 cites ~48 primary/case/practitioner FS-emptying studies in SSA, South and Southeast Asia without distinguishing the formal 37-study sample from supplemental discussion citations (including 2022 papers outside the 2002-2021 search window); (2) despite claiming to restrict to peer-reviewed journals, Section 3.2 explicitly counts grey/practitioner reports and conference papers (e.g., Eawag and Sandec 2006; Thye et al. 2009; Chowdry and Kone 2012; Hawkins et al. 2014) among the included studies; and (3) Section 3.2 states there were no experimental studies, yet Section 3.3.2 cites Peletz et al. (2020), an experimental comparison of pit-emptying services in Kisumu, Kenya. Regarding Narrow Criterion 2, the review is borderline: its primary scope is broad technological and operational challenges of FS emptying, though institutional/regulatory rules (criminalization of manual emptying, licensing/permits, unequal taxation, municipal regulation, PPP lease contracts, and tariff subsidies) constitute a substantial sub-theme (Section 3.4.5, 14/37 studies; Section 3.5.1, PPPs).
